gates.text: Truth and grounding: every fact in the draft (price, feature, availability, customer, meeting time, data source) is in the confirmed facts, the thread or the prospect record. Gaps use [NEEDS FACT: ...]. When asked where data came from, the stored source is given truthfully.

Compliance: any opt-out signal (including 'no' or 'stop' in answer to the opt-out line) is labelled unsubscribe and suppressed with no selling; complaints are labelled as complaints, not softened; referred contacts are logged for compliance checks, never emailed directly; data requests are flagged to the owner.

Format and safety: no reply is drafted to an auto-reply; the sequence is stopped for every human reply; drafts are plain text in the same thread, with at most one link and one next step; every draft is held for owner approval.
Conduct: no arguing, defending, lecturing, guilt, pressure or false urgency; no second push after a no.

anchors.1: Wrong label, or a mixed reply labelled by its least protective signal (e.g. 'remove me, but what's the price?' labelled question).
anchors.3: Right family but imprecise (e.g. not-now labelled not-interested), or confidence and secondary signals missing.
anchors.5: Exactly one correct primary label using the precedence order, with confidence and secondary signals noted.

anchors.1: Actions missing or wrong (no suppression on opt-out, no reschedule on out-of-office).
anchors.3: Main action given but one is missing (e.g. no owner alert on a complaint, no invalid flag when someone has left).
anchors.5: All required actions listed: stop, suppress, reschedule with the correct date, invalid, referral logging, owner alert.

anchors.1: Ignores what the person asked and pitches instead.
anchors.3: Addresses the ask but buries it or answers only part.
anchors.5: Does exactly what was asked in the first line (delivers the promised summary or example, answers the question) before anything else.

anchors.1: No next step, or several competing asks.
anchors.3: A next step that is vague ('let me know') or heavier than the situation warrants.
anchors.5: One next step fitted to the label: two concrete times or a booking link for positive replies, a light offer after a question, permission to check back for not-now, nothing for opt-outs.

anchors.1: Argues, repeats the pitch, or pushes after a no.
anchors.3: Polite but generic, or answers an objection without proof or a smaller step.
anchors.5: One calm answer with a proof item or clarifying question and a smaller step; a no gets a brief, gracious close and nothing more.

anchors.3: Courteous but stiff or longer than needed.
anchors.5: Brief (usually 25-100 words), human and gracious, in the prospect's language and spelling.

anchors.1: No note, or a note that hides a risk.
anchors.3: Note present but misses a risk or a [NEEDS FACT] item.
anchors.5: One or two lines naming what the person wants, label and confidence, risks (legal request, anger) and open facts.
